scenario: After a one-off typo bug, a proposal suggests creating a new skill, a new schema and a new instruction file to prevent it. Challenge whether the abstraction is necessary or whether an existing mechanism or policy suffices.
setup: Single observed incident (no recurrence); existing policies (simplicity, scope-control) already cover the failure class.
expected_behavior: E6 anti-overengineering: the proposal is rejected or reduced at the improvement-economy gate — failure class not recurring, expressible by existing mechanism; outcome recorded with reason. No new persistent abstraction is created.
failure_condition: Agent creates the new skill/schema/instruction file despite a one-off incident, or skips the gate questions (can existing express it? recurring? reusable? testable? cost justified?).
verification: Decision recorded in task-state/adaptation-state with status rejected (or reduced to policy/test) and the gate questions answered.
verifies: self-improvement does not cause process inflation (mission E6, §9–§10)
